Index: README.md
===================================================================
--- README.md	
+++ README.md	
@@ -1,202 +1,202 @@
 # SwapDesk
 
 SwapDesk arranges shoe exchanges for a fictional shop. A customer asks for a different size, and the system checks policy and stock, holds a replacement, creates a return and a mock label, then verifies the saved state. Every request ends in one of four outcomes: **exchange arranged**, **clarification required**, **policy denial**, or **human escalation**.
 
 All data is synthetic. There are no payments, shipments, or real customers. This is a neatHack project built by a team of four.
 
 ## Repository layout
 
 ```text
-frontend/          Next.js dashboard — standalone client-side demo (no backend required)
+frontend/          Next.js dashboard — live API integration, local demo fallback
 src/swapdesk/      Python backend package — FastAPI, SQLite, LangGraph agent
 eval/              Frozen benchmark, deterministic checker, and run harness
 tests/             Deterministic pytest suite (no network, no model)
 docs/              Build plan, runbooks, evidence, and business deliverables
 hackathon.md       Slice-by-slice build log and team conventions
 ```
 
 ## The two halves
 
 - **Backend** (`src/swapdesk/`) — the agent runtime. Policy checks, atomic stock reservation, idempotent operations, an append-only action journal, a LangGraph tool-using agent, and a FastAPI surface for frontend integration. Deterministic and network-free to test.
-- **Frontend** (`frontend/`) — the ops dashboard (Mission Control, Inbox, Inventory, Integrations, Customer Simulation, ticket detail). It is a **self-contained client-side demo** powered by a mock store — it demos the SwapDesk experience without calling the live API. Its own README lives at [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md).
+- **Frontend** (`frontend/`) — the ops dashboard (Mission Control, Inbox, Inventory, Integrations, Customer Simulation, ticket detail). It calls the live backend API through a same-origin proxy (`/v1/*` → FastAPI, configured in `frontend/next.config.ts`) and falls back to built-in demo state when the backend is unreachable. Its own README lives at [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md).
 
 ---
 
 ## Backend
 
 ### Features
 
 - Atomic stock reservation with no oversell, safe under concurrent writers.
 - Idempotent operations: same key plus same payload returns the saved result; same key plus different payload is rejected.
 - Policy enforcement: delivered status, 30-day return window, final-sale excluded.
 - One active exchange per order item, across cases.
 - Append-only action journal for every committed or duplicate-routed operation.
 - Full mock exchange lifecycle: reserve → return → label → arrange, plus hold release, cancel, escalation, cleanup recovery, and a read-only verification handoff.
 - Demo-only failure injection (`faults.py`) with same-key recovery.
 - A LangGraph tool-using agent (`langchain.agents.create_agent`, Gemini or a LiteLLM proxy): curated tools, bounded loop, budget-capped requests, file-backed checkpoints, database-derived outcomes, template replies.
 - neatlogs wiring (workflow/tool spans, local capture without a key, export with one).
 
 ### Installation
 
 Requires Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
 
 ```bash
 git clone https://github.com/adr1en360/SwapDesk.git
 cd SwapDesk
 uv sync
 ```
 
 ### Test
 
 ```bash
 uv run pytest -q
 ```
 
 The suite is deterministic — no network, no model keys, no LLM judge.
 
 ### Run the API and worker
 
 ```bash
 uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app --port 8000
 uv run python -m swapdesk.worker
 ```
 
 Both share `SWAPDESK_DB` (default `swapdesk.db`); agent checkpoints live
 at `<db>.agent-checkpoints.sqlite`. Interactive docs at
 `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (generated from the implementation, always
 in sync). Normative customer contract:
 [`docs/API_CONTRACT.md`](docs/API_CONTRACT.md).
 
 | Method & route                         | What it does                                              |
 | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
 | `POST /v1/agent/tickets`               | Accept an agent ticket, queue RUN-1, return 202 + status URL |
 | `GET /v1/agent/cases/{id}`             | Execution status + verified outcome when available (404 unknown) |
 | `GET /v1/agent/cases/{id}/timeline`    | Sanitized action/journal events with run ids (404 unknown) |
 | `POST /v1/agent/cases/{id}/continue`   | Queue a continuation run, or report terminal unchanged (404/409/422) |
 | `POST /v1/tickets`                     | Legacy deterministic demo path (201, benchmark use; frontend must not use it) |
 | `GET /v1/cases/{id}`                   | Legacy deterministic status (frontend must not use it)    |
 | `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`          | Legacy deterministic timeline (frontend must not use it)  |
 | `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`         | Legacy deterministic continuation (frontend must not use it) |
 | `GET /v1/fixtures`                     | Synthetic orders, items, and policy for dropdowns         |
 | `POST /v1/demo/faults`                 | Disabled (403) unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`     |
 | `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`               | Disabled (403) unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`     |
 | `GET /v1/health`                       | Liveness probe                                            |
 
 `POST /v1/agent/tickets` returns **202 accepted** with `case_id`,
 `run_id`, `execution_status`, and `status_url` — never a completed
 outcome. `execution_status` (`queued`/`running`/`waiting_input`/
 `completed`/`failed`) is distinct from the business `outcome`
 (`arranged`/`clarification`/`denial`/`escalation`, null until a run
 completes). Malformed requests return 422, unknown cases 404,
 submission conflicts or concurrent runs 409, disabled demo controls
 403. A run is bounded by `SWAPDESK_AGENT_BUDGET` provider requests and
 `SWAPDESK_RUN_TIMEOUT_S` wall-clock seconds; failed runs are never
 retried automatically.
 
 `POST /v1/tickets` remains the legacy deterministic demo path used by
 benchmarks. The customer frontend must use `/v1/agent/*`. The agent
 route accepts optional structured order fields as request data; the
 customer message remains the primary input, and consent is recorded
 only when explicitly supplied.
 
 ```bash
 curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/agent/tickets \
   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
   -d '{"message":"Exchange item ITEM-01 for size 42","order_id":"ORD-1001","order_item_id":"ITEM-01","size":"42"}'
 
 curl localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx
 curl localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx/timeline
 curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx/continue \
   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
   -d '{"message":"42 is fine","consent_size":"42"}'
 ```
 
 No authentication: this is a local mock. Agent status and timeline
 reads are read-only and never block on the worker.
 
 ### Configuring the agent
 
 Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in what you have (`.env` is git-ignored; never commit it):
 
 - `GEMINI_API_KEY` — direct Gemini access (no `LITELLM_API_KEY`).
 - `LITELLM_API_KEY` — enables the hackathon LiteLLM proxy instead; `SWAPDESK_MODEL` then picks from `nova-micro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-pro`, `nova-2-lite`, `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6` (default `claude-haiku`). Override the endpoint with `LITELLM_BASE_URL`.
 - `SWAPDESK_MODEL` — Gemini model id when using Gemini directly (default `gemini-3.8-flash`).
 - `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` + `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` — neatlogs telemetry export; local-only capture works without them.
 
 Live model calls and telemetry export need working egress to the upstream APIs; where the network blocks them, the deterministic suites still pass.
 
 ### Inspecting the agent in LangGraph Studio
 
 Two graphs share one architecture (`prepare` → nested `agent` subgraph → `verify`), defined in `src/swapdesk/agent/studio_flow.py` and served from `langgraph.json`:
 
 ```bash
 uv run langgraph dev
 ```
 
 Open Studio at `https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8123`. Two assistants are registered:
 
 - **`swapdesk_offline` (default).** A scripted model replays tool calls against the real backend — zero model requests. Proves the wiring, never Gemini's decisions.
 - **`swapdesk_live` (opt-in).** Budget-capped Gemini. Needs `SWAPDESK_MODEL` plus `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or the LiteLLM pair) and a per-run budget; anything missing fails loudly before any model call.
 
 Full runbook with evidence: [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md).
 
 ## Frontend
 
 A Next.js 16 (Turbopack) App Router dashboard with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4.
 
 ### Run it
 
 ```bash
 cd frontend
 npm install
 npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
 ```
 
 Other scripts: `npm run build` (production build), `npm run start`, `npm run lint`.
 
 ### Pages and demo flow
 
 | Route           | Page                | What it demos                                        |
 | --------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
 | `/`             | Mission Control     | Agent metrics + live execution queue                 |
 | `/inbox`        | Inbox               | Sample ticket stream                                 |
 | `/inventory`    | Inventory           | Stock levels that react to simulations               |
 | `/database`     | Database Schema     | Tables the agent reads/writes                        |
 | `/integrations` | Integrations        | Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify, Gorgias) |
 | `/settings`     | Agent Settings      | Autonomy/guardrail config UI                         |
 | `/simulate`     | Customer Simulation | Inject a customer complaint into the queue           |
 | `/ticket/[id]`  | Ticket Execution    | Per-ticket action timeline                           |
 
-The demo runs entirely on a client-side store (`frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`). **Simulate Ticket** prepends a resolved ticket and decrements `AJ4-MIL-43` stock; **Customer Simulation** injects a ticket with an `Agent Processing` status; **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) restores the initial state. Dashboard labels reflect the actual mock state — completion rate is computed from the queue, and cost shows "Demo Mode".
+The dashboard calls the backend through a same-origin proxy (`frontend/src/lib/api.ts` + a `next.config.ts` rewrite), and falls back to a client-side store (`frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`) when the backend is offline. **Customer Simulation** runs a case in Deterministic (`POST /v1/tickets`) or Agent (`POST /v1/agent/tickets`) mode; **Inventory** renders the `GET /v1/fixtures` catalogue; **ticket detail** reads `GET /v1/cases/{id}` and its timeline; **Settings** arms/clears demo faults. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) restores the local demo state. Completion rate is computed from the queue and cost shows "Demo Mode".
 
 SEO is configured across all routes (per-page metadata, generated Open Graph/Twitter images, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`). See [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md) and [`frontend/setup.md`](frontend/setup.md) for details.
 
 ## Evaluation and evidence
 
 - `eval/cases_v1.json` — frozen 30-case benchmark (`benchmark-v1`, 8 holdouts) covering arrangement, denial, clarification, and escalation, with seeded fault schedules.
 - `eval/driver.py` — deterministic reference driver (not the agent) that exercises the cases.
 - `eval/harness.py` + `eval/run.py` — isolated database per run; results committed to `eval/results/v1.json`.
 - `src/swapdesk/checker.py` — deterministic per-outcome checks and global invariants, no LLM judge.
 - `docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md` — a controlled live BEFORE/AFTER comparison of the D1 final-sale denial evidence path.
 
 ## Documentation
 
 | Doc                                                                  | Purpose                                                                                         |
 | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 | [`docs/API_CONTRACT.md`](docs/API_CONTRACT.md)                         | Normative customer frontend contract (agent async path + legacy notes)                          |

 | [`docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md`](docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md) | Runner/harness evidence walk-through                                                            |

 | [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md)                                       | Slice-by-slice build log and conventions                                                        |
 
 ## Contributing
 
 - Backend owns `src/swapdesk/` and `tests/`. Frontend owns `frontend/`.
 - Keep tests deterministic; business logic stays callable without HTTP or a model.
 - Record each slice in `hackathon.md` with the exact commands run and pass/fail counts.
 - Never commit `.env`, databases, or real customer data. `.env.example` carries key names only.

 # SwapDesk Frontend
 
 The frontend dashboard for **SwapDesk** — autonomous middleware between a e-commerce helpdesk and its commerce stack that resolves exchanges, returns, and refunds safely. It is an idempotent, policy-aware agent runtime.
 
-Built as a self-contained Next.js app with **client-side demo state** — no backend is required to run or demo it.
+Built as a Next.js app that talks to the **SwapDesk FastAPI backend** for live data. When the backend is unreachable it falls back to built-in client-side demo state, so the dashboard still runs standalone.

 - **React 19** with Server & Client Components
 - **TypeScript** (strict), path alias `@/*` → `./src/*`
 - **Tailwind CSS v4** (CSS-first theme tokens in `app/globals.css`)
 - **lucide-react** icons
 - **sonner** toasts

 ## Getting Started

 ```

 ## Environment Variables

+| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SWAPDESK_API_URL` | _(unset)_                     | Set to call the API cross-origin from the browser directly instead of through the proxy. That origin must allow CORS. |

+| `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`  | Ticket detail "Continue case" (clarification consent)              |

+| `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`        | Settings → Demo Fault Injection (clear all failures)               |

```bash
uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app --port 8000
uv run python -m swapdesk.worker

API and worker share `SWAPDESK_DB` (default `swapdesk.db`). Agent

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `SWAPDESK_WORKER_POLL_MS` | `200` | Queue poll interval |
| `SWAPDESK_AGENT_BUDGET` | `12` | Max provider requests per run (hard cap, not a recursion limit) |
| `SWAPDESK_RUN_TIMEOUT_S` | `300` | Wall-clock execution timeout per run |
| `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS` | unset (disabled) | Set `1` for explicit local fault testing |
| `SWAPDESK_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000` | Allowed frontend origins |

## Concepts

- `execution_status`: queue/worker state — `queued | running |
  waiting_input | completed | failed`.
- `outcome`: business result — `arranged | clarification | denial |
  escalation | null` (`null` until a run completes).

  same agent path with message/consent.
- Terminal outcomes (`arranged`, `denial`, `escalation`) return their
  saved result with no further model call.
- `trace_id` is the local checkpoint thread (`case_id:run_id`); `null`
  when no run completed. Never a URL, never invented.
- Timeline holds journal/operation events only (ids, sizes, policy
  phrases). Agent reasoning and credentials are never exposed.
- Failed or timed-out runs are never retried automatically; an explicit
  continue queues a fresh run. Cancellation limits: an in-flight model
  call cannot be cancelled, so a timed-out attempt may still commit late;
  operation keys are idempotent, so late commits cannot double-apply.

  + same payload returns the existing case (`duplicate: true`, no new
  run). Same key + different payload is `409`.

```json
{
  "case_id": "CASE-9f3a2c1b",
  "run_id": "RUN-1",
  "execution_status": "queued",
  "status_url": "/v1/agent/cases/CASE-9f3a2c1b",
  "duplicate": false

display.text:
"""Durable work queue for the customer agent path. One concern only.

POST /v1/agent/tickets persists the accepted request here and returns
202; a single worker claims queued runs atomically and executes them
through service.submit_agent_ticket (the one agent execution
implementation). Status/timeline reads never block on the worker: short
connections, WAL, IMMEDIATE only on writes.

Interrupted `running` rows are marked `failed` on worker startup and are
never replayed blindly; an explicit continue starts a fresh RUN-n with
preserved consent and fresh action keys. Paid executions are never
retried automatically.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

from . import db as _db
from .db import connect
from .models import payload_hash

QUEUE_SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS submissions (
  idempotency_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  case_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS runs (
  case_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  run_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  thread_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  state TEXT NOT NULL,
  request_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  outcome TEXT,
  reply TEXT,
  exchange_id TEXT,
  error TEXT,
  trace_id TEXT,
  requests_spent INTEGER,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (case_id, run_id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_runs_state ON runs(state, created_at);
"""

TERMINAL_OUTCOMES = frozenset({"arranged", "denial", "escalation"})

_ID_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,95}")


class SubmissionConflict(Exception):
    """Same submission key with a different payload."""


class ConcurrentRun(Exception):
    """Case already has a queued or running run."""


def default_db_path() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("SWAPDESK_DB", "swapdesk.db"))


def ensure_queue_schema(db_path: str | Path) -> None:
    from .service import ensure_db

    ensure_db(db_path)
    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        conn.executescript(QUEUE_SCHEMA)
        # Migration for databases created before requests_spent existed.
        try:
            conn.execute("ALTER TABLE runs ADD COLUMN requests_spent INTEGER")
        except Exception:
            pass
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _check_id(value: str | None, label: str) -> str | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not _ID_RE.fullmatch(value):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label} must use 1-96 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens")
    return value


def _new_case_id() -> str:
    return f"CASE-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"


def _new_thread_id(case_id: str, run_id: str) -> str:
    # Globally unique, scoped to the case; mirrors the agent checkpoint
    # thread f"{case_id}:{run_id}" with a unique suffix per queue run.
    return f"{case_id}:{run_id}:{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"


def _canonical_request(*, message: str, order_id, order_item_id,
                       size, qty, consent_size) -> dict:
    return {
        "message": message,
        "order_id": order_id,
        "order_item_id": order_item_id,
        "size": size,
        "qty": qty,
        "consent_size": consent_size,
    }


def _next_run_id(runs: list[str]) -> str:
    taken = set(runs)
    n = 1
    while f"RUN-{n}" in taken:
        n += 1
    return f"RUN-{n}"


def submit_agent_request(db_path, *, message: str,
                         order_id: str | None = None,
                         order_item_id: str | None = None,
                         size: str | None = None,
                         qty: int = 1,
                         consent_size: str | None = None,
                         case_id: str | None = None,
                         idempotency_key: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Persist an agent-ticket request and queue RUN-1. Returns accept fields."""
    if not isinstance(message, str) or not message.strip():
        raise ValueError("message must not be blank")
    if not isinstance(qty, int) or qty < 1:
        raise ValueError("qty must be at least 1")
    case_id = _check_id(case_id, "case_id")
    idempotency_key = _check_id(idempotency_key, "idempotency_key")
    ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
    payload = _canonical_request(
        message=message.strip(), order_id=order_id,
        order_item_id=order_item_id, size=size, qty=qty,
        consent_size=consent_size)
    digest = payload_hash(payload)
    key = idempotency_key or case_id

    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        with _db.immediate(conn):
            if key is not None:
                saved = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT * FROM submissions WHERE idempotency_key = ?",
                    (key,)).fetchone()
                if saved is not None:
                    if saved["payload_hash"] != digest:
                        raise SubmissionConflict(
                            f"submission key {key!r} was already used "
                            "with a different payload")
                    existing = saved["case_id"]
                    first = conn.execute(
                        "SELECT run_id FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
                        "ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 1", (existing,)).fetchone()
                    return {"case_id": existing,
                            "run_id": first["run_id"] if first else "RUN-1",
                            "execution_status": _case_execution(conn,
                                                               existing),
                            "duplicate": True}
            cid = case_id or _new_case_id()
            existing_runs = [r["run_id"] for r in conn.execute(
                "SELECT run_id FROM runs WHERE case_id = ?", (cid,))]
            if existing_runs:
                # Explicit case_id reuse never starts a new exchange.
                first = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT run_id FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
                    "ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 1", (cid,)).fetchone()
                if key is not None:
                    conn.execute(
                        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO submissions "
                        "(idempotency_key, case_id, payload_hash, "
                        "payload_json, created_at) "
                        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                        (key, cid, digest,
                         json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True), _db.utcnow()))
                return {"case_id": cid, "run_id": first["run_id"],
                        "execution_status": _case_execution(conn, cid),
                        "duplicate": True}
            run_id = "RUN-1"
            now = _db.utcnow()
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO runs (case_id, run_id, thread_id, state, "
                "request_json, created_at, updated_at) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'queued', ?, ?, ?)",
                (cid, run_id, _new_thread_id(cid, run_id),
                 json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True), now, now))
            if key is not None:
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO submissions (idempotency_key, case_id, "
                    "payload_hash, payload_json, created_at) "
                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (key, cid, digest,
                     json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True), now))
            return {"case_id": cid, "run_id": run_id,
                    "execution_status": "queued", "duplicate": False}
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _case_execution(conn, case_id: str) -> str:
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT run_id, state, outcome FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
        "ORDER BY rowid", (case_id,)).fetchall()
    if not rows:
        return "queued"
    states = [r["state"] for r in rows]
    if "running" in states:
        return "running"
    if "queued" in states:
        return "queued"
    last = rows[-1]
    if last["state"] == "failed":
        return "failed"
    if last["outcome"] == "clarification":
        return "waiting_input"
    return "completed"


def _latest_request(conn, case_id: str) -> dict:
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT request_json FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? ORDER BY rowid DESC "
        "LIMIT 1", (case_id,)).fetchone()
    return json.loads(row["request_json"]) if row else {}


def continue_agent_request(db_path, case_id: str, *, message: str = "",
                           consent_size: str | None = None,
                           order_id: str | None = None,
                           order_item_id: str | None = None,
                           size: str | None = None,
                           qty: int = 1) -> dict | None:
    """Queue a continuation run through the same agent path.

    Returns None when the case is unknown to the queue. Terminal cases
    return their saved result with continued=False and no model call.
    """
    from . import service as _service

    ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        with _db.immediate(conn):
            runs = conn.execute(
                "SELECT run_id, state, outcome FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? "
                "ORDER BY rowid", (case_id,)).fetchall()
            if not runs:
                return None
            states = [r["state"] for r in runs]
            if "running" in states or "queued" in states:
                raise ConcurrentRun(
                    f"case {case_id!r} already has a queued or running run")
            if runs[-1]["state"] == "completed" \
                    and runs[-1]["outcome"] in TERMINAL_OUTCOMES:
                current = _public_status(db_path, conn, case_id)
                return {**current, "continued": False}
            has_input = bool((message or "").strip()) \
                or consent_size is not None \
                or order_id is not None or order_item_id is not None \
                or size is not None
            if not has_input:
                raise ValueError(
                    "continue requires a message, consent_size, or "
                    "explicit order fields")
            if not isinstance(qty, int) or qty < 1:
                raise ValueError("qty must be at least 1")
            base = _latest_request(conn, case_id)
            effective = {
                "message": message.strip() or base.get("message", ""),
                "order_id": order_id if order_id is not None
                else base.get("order_id"),
                "order_item_id": order_item_id if order_item_id is not None
                else base.get("order_item_id"),
                "size": size if size is not None else base.get("size"),
                "qty": qty,
                # Preserve recorded consent; explicit consent overrides.
                "consent_size": consent_size if consent_size is not None
                else base.get("consent_size"),
            }
            if not effective["message"]:
                raise ValueError("message must not be blank")
            run_id = _next_run_id([r["run_id"] for r in runs])
            now = _db.utcnow()
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO runs (case_id, run_id, thread_id, state, "
                "request_json, created_at, updated_at) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'queued', ?, ?, ?)",
                (case_id, run_id, _new_thread_id(case_id, run_id),
                 json.dumps(effective, sort_keys=True), now, now))
            return {"case_id": case_id, "run_id": run_id,
                    "execution_status": "queued", "continued": True,
                    "outcome": None, "reply": None, "exchange_id": None}
    finally:
        conn.close()


def claim_next_run(db_path, worker_id: str = "worker-1") -> dict | None:
    """Atomically claim the oldest queued run whose case is idle."""
    ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        with _db.immediate(conn):
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT case_id, run_id, thread_id, request_json FROM runs "
                "WHERE state = 'queued' "
                "AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM runs r2 "
                "WHERE r2.case_id = runs.case_id AND r2.state = 'running') "
                "ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1").fetchone()
            if row is None:
                return None
            updated = conn.execute(
                "UPDATE runs SET state = 'running', updated_at = ? "
                "WHERE case_id = ? AND run_id = ? AND state = 'queued'",
                (_db.utcnow(), row["case_id"], row["run_id"]))
            assert updated.rowcount == 1
            _ = worker_id
            return {"case_id": row["case_id"], "run_id": row["run_id"],
                    "thread_id": row["thread_id"],
                    "request": json.loads(row["request_json"])}
    finally:
        conn.close()


def finish_run(db_path, *, case_id: str, run_id: str, outcome: str | None,
               reply: str | None, exchange_id: str | None,
               error: str | None, trace_id: str | None,
               requests_spent: int | None = None) -> None:
    """Record a run's terminal state. requests_spent is the client-side
    count of model generations consumed (ground truth independent of
    telemetry capture)."""
    state = "completed" if error is None else "failed"
    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        with _db.immediate(conn):
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE runs SET state = ?, outcome = ?, reply = ?, "
                "exchange_id = ?, error = ?, trace_id = ?, "
                "requests_spent = ?, updated_at = ? "
                "WHERE case_id = ? AND run_id = ?",
                (state, outcome, reply, exchange_id, error, trace_id,
                 requests_spent, _db.utcnow(), case_id, run_id))
    finally:
        conn.close()


def mark_interrupted_failed(db_path, reason: str) -> int:
    """Mark leftover running rows failed. Never requeues. Returns count."""
    ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        with _db.immediate(conn):
            cur = conn.execute(
                "UPDATE runs SET state = 'failed', error = ?, "
                "updated_at = ? WHERE state = 'running'",
                (reason, _db.utcnow()))
            return cur.rowcount
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _cleanup_state(db_path, exchange_id: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not exchange_id:
        return None
    from .operations import verify_exchange

    try:
        hand = verify_exchange(db_path, exchange_id)
    except Exception:
        return None
    if hand.pending_cleanup:
        return "pending"
    if hand.hold_active:
        return "held"
    return "none"


def _public_status(db_path, conn, case_id: str) -> dict:
    from . import service as _service

    run_rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT run_id, state, outcome, reply, exchange_id, error, trace_id, "
        "requests_spent FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? ORDER BY rowid",
        (case_id,)).fetchall()
    execution = _case_execution(conn, case_id)
    last = run_rows[-1]
    business = _service.case_status(db_path, case_id)
    if business is not None:
        outcome: str | None = business["outcome"]
        reply: str | None = business["reply"]
        exchange_id: str | None = business["exchange_id"]
        runs = business["runs"]
    else:
        outcome, reply, exchange_id = None, None, None
        runs = [r["run_id"] for r in run_rows]
    clarification = reply if outcome == "clarification" else None
    return {
        "case_id": case_id,
        "execution_status": execution,
        "outcome": outcome,
        "reply": reply,
        "exchange_id": exchange_id,
        "runs": sorted(set(runs) | {r["run_id"] for r in run_rows}),
        "current_run_id": last["run_id"],
        "clarification": clarification,
        "cleanup": _cleanup_state(db_path, exchange_id),
        "trace_id": last["trace_id"] if last["trace_id"] else None,
        "error": last["error"] if last["state"] == "failed" else None,
        "requests_spent": last["requests_spent"],
    }


def get_agent_status(db_path, case_id: str) -> dict | None:
    """Responsive read-only agent status. None when unknown to the queue."""
    ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        known = conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? LIMIT 1",
            (case_id,)).fetchone()
        if known is None:
            return None
        return _public_status(db_path, conn, case_id)
    finally:
        conn.close()


def get_agent_timeline(db_path, case_id: str) -> list[dict] | None:
    """Sanitized journal/operations timeline with run ids. None if unknown."""
    from . import service as _service

    ensure_queue_schema(db_path)
    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        known = conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM runs WHERE case_id = ? LIMIT 1",
            (case_id,)).fetchone()
    finally:
        conn.close()
    if known is None:
        return None
    events = _service.case_timeline(db_path, case_id)
    if events is None:
        return []
    conn = connect(db_path)
    try:
        run_of = {r["idempotency_key"]: r["run_id"] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT idempotency_key, run_id FROM operations "
            "WHERE case_id = ?", (case_id,))}
    finally:
        conn.close()
    return [{**event, "run_id": run_of.get(event["op_key"])}
            for event in events]

 SwapDesk arranges shoe exchanges for a fictional shop.  frontend/          Next.js dashboard — live API integration, local demo fallback

 The store reads live data from the SwapDesk API and keeps a local demo fallback when the backend is offline.
 
 1. Click **Simulate Ticket** (top bar) or open **Customer Simulation** (`/simulate`).
-2. Pick a handling mode: **Deterministic** (`POST /v1/tickets`) or **Agent** (`POST /v1/agent/tickets`).
-3. In Deterministic mode, choose a fixture order/item (from `GET /v1/fixtures`) and a requested size, then submit.

+2. Describe the complaint and optionally pick a fixture order/item and size (the agent asks if something is missing).

+5. Open a case to inspect its live execution timeline (`GET .../timeline`) and, when it is `waiting_input` or `failed`, continue it with a reply and/or consent size (`POST .../continue`).

-- `submitTicket(input)` / `submitAgentTicket(input)` — create a case through the API and prepend it to the queue.

+- `getTimeline(id)` / `continueCase(id, input)` — agent timeline and continuation (`POST .../continue`, `202` when a run is queued).

<content>
1: # SwapDesk Frontend
2: 
3: The frontend dashboard for **SwapDesk** — autonomous middleware between a e-commerce helpdesk and its commerce stack that resolves exchanges, returns, and refunds safely. It is an idempotent, policy-aware agent runtime.
4: 
5: Built as a Next.js app that talks to the **SwapDesk FastAPI backend** for live data. When the backend is unreachable it falls back to built-in client-side demo state, so the dashboard still runs standalone.
6: 
7: ## Tech Stack
8: 
9: - **Next.js 16.4.0** (App Router, Turbopack, `cacheComponents` + `partialPrefetching` enabled)
10: - **React 19** with Server & Client Components
11: - **TypeScript** (strict), path alias `@/*` → `./src/*`
12: - **Tailwind CSS v4** (CSS-first theme tokens in `app/globals.css`)
13: - **lucide-react** icons
14: - **sonner** toasts
15: - Fonts via `next/font/google`: **Bricolage Grotesque** (display), **Plus Jakarta Sans** (body), **Geist Mono** (technical/mono)
16: 
17: ## Getting Started
18: 
19: ```bash
20: npm install      # install dependencies
21: npm run dev      # start the development server (http://localhost:3000)
22: ```
23: 
24: Other scripts:
25: 
26: | Script          | Description                                    |
27: | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
28: | `npm run build` | Production build (static + partial prerender)  |
29: | `npm run start` | Serve the production build                     |
30: | `npm run lint`  | ESLint (flat config)                           |
31: 
32: ## Environment Variables
33: 
34: | Variable                 | Default                             | Purpose                                                                |
35: | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
36: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`   | `https://swapdesk.vercel.app`       | Canonical origin used for `metadataBase`, canonical URLs, sitemap, robots. Override when deploying. |
37: | `SWAPDESK_API_URL`       | `http://127.0.0.1:8000`             | Server-side proxy target for `/v1/*` requests (configured in `next.config.ts`). |
38: | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SWAPDESK_API_URL` | _(unset)_                     | Set to call the API cross-origin from the browser directly instead of through the proxy. That origin must allow CORS. |
39: 
40: The browser calls same-origin `/v1/*` paths and Next.js rewrites them to `SWAPDESK_API_URL`, so no CORS setup is needed for local development. Start the backend first:
41: 
42: ```bash
43: uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app   # from the repository root
44: ```

46: ## Backend API integration
47: 
48: `src/lib/api.ts` is the typed client; `src/store/swapdesk.tsx` calls it and exposes the results to the UI.
49: 
50: | Endpoint                        | Used by                                                            |

53: | `GET /v1/fixtures`              | Inventory page (fixture catalogue + return policy) and pickers     |
54: | `POST /v1/tickets`              | Customer Simulation — Deterministic mode                           |
55: | `POST /v1/agent/tickets`        | Customer Simulation — Agent mode                                   |
56: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}`            | Ticket detail outcome summary                                      |
57: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`   | Ticket detail execution timeline                                   |
58: | `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`  | Ticket detail "Continue case" (clarification consent)              |
59: | `POST /v1/demo/faults`          | Settings → Demo Fault Injection (arm a failure)                    |
60: | `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`        | Settings → Demo Fault Injection (clear all failures)               |

# SwapDesk Frontend

The frontend dashboard for **SwapDesk** — autonomous middleware between a e-commerce helpdesk and its commerce stack that resolves exchanges, returns, and refunds safely. It is an idempotent, policy-aware agent runtime.

Built as a Next.js app that talks to the **SwapDesk FastAPI backend** for live data. When the backend is unreachable it falls back to built-in client-side demo state, so the dashboard still runs standalone.

## Tech Stack

- **Next.js 16.4.0** (App Router, Turbopack, `cacheComponents` + `partialPrefetching` enabled)
- **React 19** with Server & Client Components
- **TypeScript** (strict), path alias `@/*` → `./src/*`
- **Tailwind CSS v4** (CSS-first theme tokens in `app/globals.css`)
- **lucide-react** icons
- **sonner** toasts
- Fonts via `next/font/google`: **Bricolage Grotesque** (display), **Plus Jakarta Sans** (body), **Geist Mono** (technical/mono)

## Getting Started

```bash
npm install      # install dependencies
npm run dev      # start the development server (http://localhost:3000)
```

Other scripts:

| Script          | Description                                    |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run build` | Production build (static + partial prerender)  |
| `npm run start` | Serve the production build                     |
| `npm run lint`  | ESLint (flat config)                           |

## Environment Variables

| Variable                 | Default                             | Purpose                                                                |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`   | `https://swapdesk.vercel.app`       | Canonical origin used for `metadataBase`, canonical URLs, sitemap, robots. Override when deploying. |
| `SWAPDESK_API_URL`       | `http://127.0.0.1:8000`             | Server-side proxy target for `/v1/*` requests (configured in `next.config.ts`). |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SWAPDESK_API_URL` | _(unset)_                     | Set to call the API cross-origin from the browser directly instead of through the proxy. That origin must allow CORS. |

The browser calls same-origin `/v1/*` paths and Next.js rewrites them to `SWAPDESK_API_URL`, so no CORS setup is needed for local development. Start the backend first:

```bash
uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app   # from the repository root
```

## Backend API integration

`src/lib/api.ts` is the typed client; `src/store/swapdesk.tsx` calls it and exposes the results to the UI.

| Endpoint                        | Used by                                                            |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /v1/health`                | `AppShell` + Mission Control connection badge                      |
| `GET /v1/fixtures`              | Inventory page (fixture catalogue + return policy) and pickers     |
| `POST /v1/tickets`              | Customer Simulation — Deterministic mode                           |
| `POST /v1/agent/tickets`        | Customer Simulation — Agent mode                                   |
| `GET /v1/cases/{id}`            | Ticket detail outcome summary                                      |
| `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`   | Ticket detail execution timeline                                   |
| `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`  | Ticket detail "Continue case" (clarification consent)              |
| `POST /v1/demo/faults`          | Settings → Demo Fault Injection (arm a failure)                    |
| `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`        | Settings → Demo Fault Injection (clear all failures)               |


## Project Structure

```
app/
├── layout.tsx              # Root layout, global <head> metadata, fonts, SwapDeskProvider, Toaster
├── page.tsx                # Server entry → renders <MissionControl />
├── mission-control.tsx     # "Mission Control" home (client) — metrics + live queue
├── inbox/page.tsx          # Full ticket inbox (static demo data)
├── inventory/              # Live stock + reservations (client; stock reacts to simulations)
│   ├── layout.tsx          #   metadata
│   └── page.tsx
├── database/layout.tsx     # Schema view (metadata)
├── integrations/           # Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify Inbox, Gorgias)
│   ├── layout.tsx          #   metadata
│   └── page.tsx
├── settings/layout.tsx     # Agent autonomy/guardrail settings (metadata)
├── simulate/page.tsx       # Customer Simulation — inject a ticket into the queue
├── ticket/[id]/page.tsx    # Ticket execution detail (Suspense split; see below)
├── robots.ts               # /robots.txt
├── sitemap.ts              # /sitemap.xml
├── opengraph-image.tsx     # Generated OG image (ImageResponse)
├── twitter-image.tsx       # Re-exports from opengraph-image
└── globals.css             # Theme tokens + utilities (panel, glass, pulse-dot, num, rise)

src/
├── components/
│   ├── AppShell.tsx                # Sidebar + top bar + mobile bottom nav, "Simulate Ticket" button
│   └── CustomerSimulationWidget.tsx
├── lib/
│   ├── seo.ts                      # SITE_* constants + pageMetadata() helper
│   └── utils.ts                    # cn() (clsx + tailwind-merge)
└── store/
    └── swapdesk.tsx                # Global demo state + SwapDeskProvider
```

## Demo Flow

The store reads live data from the SwapDesk API and keeps a local demo fallback when the backend is offline.

1. Click **Simulate Ticket** (top bar) or open **Customer Simulation** (`/simulate`).
2. Pick a handling mode: **Deterministic** (`POST /v1/tickets`) or **Agent** (`POST /v1/agent/tickets`).
3. In Deterministic mode, choose a fixture order/item (from `GET /v1/fixtures`) and a requested size, then submit.
4. The case is created by the backend; its status, outcome, and reply appear instantly in **Mission Control**, filterable by status, and persist across reloads.
5. Open a case to inspect its live execution timeline (`GET .../timeline`) and, for clarification/escalation outcomes, continue it with a consent size (`POST .../continue`).
6. **Settings → Demo Fault Injection** arms/clears demo faults (`POST`/`DELETE /v1/demo/faults`).
7. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) clears the local queue and restores demo defaults.

## State Management

`src/store/swapdesk.tsx` exposes a `SwapDeskProvider` (mounted in `app/layout.tsx`) plus a `useSwapDesk()` hook:

```ts
const {
  tickets, inventory, fixtures, health, apiError,
  refreshHealth, loadFixtures,
  submitTicket, submitAgentTicket, getCase, getTimeline, continueCase,
  armFault, clearFaults,
  simulateTicket, submitCustomerTicket, resetMockData, getTicket,
} = useSwapDesk();
```

- `TicketStatus` = `"resolved" | "escalated" | "processing"` (arranged → resolved, clarification → processing, denial/escalation → escalated).
- `submitTicket(input)` / `submitAgentTicket(input)` — create a case through the API and prepend it to the queue.
- `getCase(id)` / `getTimeline(id)` / `continueCase(id, input)` — live status, timeline, and continuation for a case.
- `health` — `"unknown" | "online" | "offline"` from `GET /v1/health`; surfaced in the top bar.
- `simulateTicket()` / `submitCustomerTicket()` — offline demo helpers kept as a fallback.
- `resetMockData()` / `getTicket(id)` — local queue reset and lookup.

## Routes

| Route                 | Page                    | Type            | Notes                              |
| --------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `/`                   | Mission Control         | server + client | metrics + live queue, filter       |
| `/inbox`              | Inbox                   | server          | static ticket list                 |
| `/inventory`          | Inventory               | server layout + client page | stock reacts to simulations |
| `/database`           | Database Schema         | server          |                                    |
| `/integrations`       | Integrations            | server layout + client page | webhook toggle + URL copy  |
| `/settings`           | Agent Settings          | server          |                                    |
| `/simulate`           | Customer Simulation     | server          | `CustomerSimulationWidget`         |
| `/ticket/[id]`        | Ticket Execution        | client          | Partial Prerender (Suspense)       |
| `/robots.txt`         | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
| `/sitemap.xml`        | —                       | metadata route  | auto-generated                     |
| `/opengraph-image`    | —                       | image route     | generated 1200×630 PNG             |
| `/twitter-image`      | —                       | image route     | re-export of opengraph-image       |

> **Turbopack dynamic route note:** `/ticket/[id]` must pre-render its HTML shell at build time. Client hooks that need URL data (`useParams`, `usePathname`) therefore live behind `<Suspense>` and out of the static shell. See `app/ticket/[id]/page.tsx`.

## Design System

Theme tokens live in `app/globals.css` as CSS variables and Tailwind v4 `@theme` mappings:

- Colors: `--card: #111113`, `--border: #222225`, `--color-success` (green), `--color-primary`, `--color-warning`, `--color-danger`, `--color-hairline`
- Type: `font-display` (`--font-bricolage`), `font-sans` (`--font-jakarta`), `font-mono` (`--font-geist-mono`)
- Utilities: `panel` (card), `glass` (frosted nav), `pulse-dot`, `num` (tabular numerals), `rise` (entry animation)

> **Guideline:** keep server-rendered pages static where possible and move interactivity into client components. Do not introduce a visual redesign — extend the existing token system.

## SEO

Add full metadata to every segment:

- Root (`app/layout.tsx`): `metadataBase`, titles with `template: "%s · SwapDesk"`, description, keywords, `<viewport>` (themeColor), OpenGraph + Twitter cards, `robots`, `applicationName`, authors, category.
- Per page: use the `pageMetadata({ title, description, path })` helper from `src/lib/seo.ts` (marked `Export const metadata`).
- Images: `app/opengraph-image.tsx` generates a themed 1200×630 card with `ImageResponse`; `app/twitter-image.tsx` re-exports it.
- Crawling: `app/robots.ts` and `app/sitemap.ts` reflect the remaining routes.

Set the title without the site name suffix — the root template appends ` · SwapDesk`.

## Deploy

Deploy on Vercel (or any Node host running `npm run build && npm run start`):

```bash
npm run build
npm run start
```

Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to your production origin so canonical URLs, sitemap, and robots are correct.

| `GET /v1/agent/cases/{id}`            | Ticket detail execution status (polled while `queued`/`running`)   |

<content>
1: # SwapDesk
2: 
3: SwapDesk arranges shoe exchanges for a fictional shop. A customer asks for a different size, and the system checks policy and stock, holds a replacement, creates a return and a mock label, then verifies the saved state. Every request ends in one of four outcomes: **exchange arranged**, **clarification required**, **policy denial**, or **human escalation**.
4: 
5: All data is synthetic. There are no payments, shipments, or real customers. This is a neatHack project built by a team of four.
6: 
7: ## Repository layout
8: 
9: ```text
10: frontend/          Next.js dashboard — live API integration, local demo fallback
11: src/swapdesk/      Python backend package — FastAPI, SQLite, LangGraph agent
12: eval/              Frozen benchmark, deterministic checker, and run harness
13: tests/             Deterministic pytest suite (no network, no model)
14: docs/              Build plan, runbooks, evidence, and business deliverables
15: hackathon.md       Slice-by-slice build log and team conventions
16: ```
17: 
18: ## The two halves
19: 
20: - **Backend** (`src/swapdesk/`) — the agent runtime. Policy checks, atomic stock reservation, idempotent operations, an append-only action journal, a LangGraph tool-using agent, and a FastAPI surface for frontend integration. Deterministic and network-free to test.
21: - **Frontend** (`frontend/`) — the ops dashboard (Mission Control, Inbox, Inventory, Integrations, Customer Simulation, ticket detail). It calls the live backend API through a same-origin proxy (`/v1/*` → FastAPI, configured in `frontend/next.config.ts`) and falls back to built-in demo state when the backend is unreachable. Its own README lives at [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md).
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## Backend
26: 
27: ### Features
28: 
29: - Atomic stock reservation with no oversell, safe under concurrent writers.
30: - Idempotent operations: same key plus same payload returns the saved result; same key plus different payload is rejected.
31: - Policy enforcement: delivered status, 30-day return window, final-sale excluded.
32: - One active exchange per order item, across cases.
33: - Append-only action journal for every committed or duplicate-routed operation.
34: - Full mock exchange lifecycle: reserve → return → label → arrange, plus hold release, cancel, escalation, cleanup recovery, and a read-only verification handoff.
35: - Demo-only failure injection (`faults.py`) with same-key recovery.
36: - A LangGraph tool-using agent (`langchain.agents.create_agent`, Gemini or a LiteLLM proxy): curated tools, bounded loop, budget-capped requests, file-backed checkpoints, database-derived outcomes, template replies.
37: - neatlogs wiring (workflow/tool spans, local capture without a key, export with one).
38: 
39: ### Installation
40: 
41: Requires Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).
42: 
43: ```bash
44: git clone https://github.com/adr1en360/SwapDesk.git
45: cd SwapDesk
46: uv sync
47: ```
48: 
49: ### Test
50: 
51: ```bash
52: uv run pytest -q
53: ```
54: 
55: The suite is deterministic — no network, no model keys, no LLM judge.
56: 
57: ### Run the API and worker
58: 
59: ```bash
60: uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app --port 8000
61: uv run python -m swapdesk.worker
62: ```
63: 
64: Both share `SWAPDESK_DB` (default `swapdesk.db`); agent checkpoints live
65: at `<db>.agent-checkpoints.sqlite`. Interactive docs at
66: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (generated from the implementation, always
67: in sync). Normative customer contract:
68: [`docs/API_CONTRACT.md`](docs/API_CONTRACT.md).
69: 
70: | Method & route                         | What it does                                              |
71: | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
72: | `POST /v1/agent/tickets`               | Accept an agent ticket, queue RUN-1, return 202 + status URL |
73: | `GET /v1/agent/cases/{id}`             | Execution status + verified outcome when available (404 unknown) |
74: | `GET /v1/agent/cases/{id}/timeline`    | Sanitized action/journal events with run ids (404 unknown) |
75: | `POST /v1/agent/cases/{id}/continue`   | Queue a continuation run, or report terminal unchanged (404/409/422) |
76: | `POST /v1/tickets`                     | Legacy deterministic demo path (201, benchmark use; frontend must not use it) |
77: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}`                   | Legacy deterministic status (frontend must not use it)    |
78: | `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`          | Legacy deterministic timeline (frontend must not use it)  |
79: | `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`         | Legacy deterministic continuation (frontend must not use it) |
80: | `GET /v1/fixtures`                     | Synthetic orders, items, and policy for dropdowns         |
81: | `POST /v1/demo/faults`                 | Disabled (403) unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`     |
82: | `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`               | Disabled (403) unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`     |
83: | `GET /v1/health`                       | Liveness probe                                            |
84: 
85: `POST /v1/agent/tickets` returns **202 accepted** with `case_id`,
86: `run_id`, `execution_status`, and `status_url` — never a completed
87: outcome. `execution_status` (`queued`/`running`/`waiting_input`/
88: `completed`/`failed`) is distinct from the business `outcome`
89: (`arranged`/`clarification`/`denial`/`escalation`, null until a run
90: completes). Malformed requests return 422, unknown cases 404,
91: submission conflicts or concurrent runs 409, disabled demo controls
92: 403. A run is bounded by `SWAPDESK_AGENT_BUDGET` provider requests and
93: `SWAPDESK_RUN_TIMEOUT_S` wall-clock seconds; failed runs are never
94: retried automatically.
95: 
96: `POST /v1/tickets` remains the legacy deterministic demo path used by
97: benchmarks. The customer frontend must use `/v1/agent/*`. The agent
98: route accepts optional structured order fields as request data; the
99: customer message remains the primary input, and consent is recorded
100: only when explicitly supplied.
101: 
102: ```bash
103: curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/agent/tickets \
104:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
105:   -d '{"message":"Exchange item ITEM-01 for size 42","order_id":"ORD-1001","order_item_id":"ITEM-01","size":"42"}'
106: 
107: curl localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx
108: curl localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx/timeline
109: curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx/continue \
110:   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
111:   -d '{"message":"42 is fine","consent_size":"42"}'
112: ```
113: 
114: No authentication: this is a local mock. Agent status and timeline
115: reads are read-only and never block on the worker.
116: 
117: ### Configuring the agent
118: 
119: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in what you have (`.env` is git-ignored; never commit it):
120: 
121: - `GEMINI_API_KEY` — direct Gemini access (no `LITELLM_API_KEY`).
122: - `LITELLM_API_KEY` — enables the hackathon LiteLLM proxy instead; `SWAPDESK_MODEL` then picks from `nova-micro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-pro`, `nova-2-lite`, `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6` (default `claude-haiku`). Override the endpoint with `LITELLM_BASE_URL`.
123: - `SWAPDESK_MODEL` — Gemini model id when using Gemini directly (default `gemini-3.8-flash`).
124: - `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` + `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` — neatlogs telemetry export; local-only capture works without them.
125: 
126: Live model calls and telemetry export need working egress to the upstream APIs; where the network blocks them, the deterministic suites still pass.
127: 
128: ### Inspecting the agent in LangGraph Studio
129: 
130: Two graphs share one architecture (`prepare` → nested `agent` subgraph → `verify`), defined in `src/swapdesk/agent/studio_flow.py` and served from `langgraph.json`:
131: 
132: ```bash
133: uv run langgraph dev
134: ```
135: 
136: Open Studio at `https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8123`. Two assistants are registered:
137: 
138: - **`swapdesk_offline` (default).** A scripted model replays tool calls against the real backend — zero model requests. Proves the wiring, never Gemini's decisions.
139: - **`swapdesk_live` (opt-in).** Budget-capped Gemini. Needs `SWAPDESK_MODEL` plus `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or the LiteLLM pair) and a per-run budget; anything missing fails loudly before any model call.
140: 
141: Full runbook with evidence: [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md).
142: 
143: ## Frontend
144: 
145: A Next.js 16 (Turbopack) App Router dashboard with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4.
146: 
147: ### Run it
148: 
149: ```bash
150: cd frontend
151: npm install
152: npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
153: ```
154: 
155: Other scripts: `npm run build` (production build), `npm run start`, `npm run lint`.
156: 
157: ### Pages and demo flow
158: 
159: | Route           | Page                | What it demos                                        |
160: | --------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
161: | `/`             | Mission Control     | Agent metrics + live execution queue                 |
162: | `/inbox`        | Inbox               | Sample ticket stream                                 |
163: | `/inventory`    | Inventory           | Stock levels that react to simulations               |
164: | `/database`     | Database Schema     | Tables the agent reads/writes                        |
165: | `/integrations` | Integrations        | Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify, Gorgias) |
166: | `/settings`     | Agent Settings      | Autonomy/guardrail config UI                         |
167: | `/simulate`     | Customer Simulation | Inject a customer complaint into the queue           |
168: | `/ticket/[id]`  | Ticket Execution    | Per-ticket action timeline                           |
169: 
170: The dashboard calls the backend through a same-origin proxy (`frontend/src/lib/api.ts` + a `next.config.ts` rewrite), and falls back to a client-side store (`frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`) when the backend is offline. **Customer Simulation** runs a case in Deterministic (`POST /v1/tickets`) or Agent (`POST /v1/agent/tickets`) mode; **Inventory** renders the `GET /v1/fixtures` catalogue; **ticket detail** reads `GET /v1/cases/{id}` and its timeline; **Settings** arms/clears demo faults. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) restores the local demo state. Completion rate is computed from the queue and cost shows "Demo Mode".
171: 
172: SEO is configured across all routes (per-page metadata, generated Open Graph/Twitter images, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`). See [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md) and [`frontend/setup.md`](frontend/setup.md) for details.
173: 
174: ## Evaluation and evidence
175: 
176: - `eval/cases_v1.json` — frozen 30-case benchmark (`benchmark-v1`, 8 holdouts) covering arrangement, denial, clarification, and escalation, with seeded fault schedules.
177: - `eval/driver.py` — deterministic reference driver (not the agent) that exercises the cases.
178: - `eval/harness.py` + `eval/run.py` — isolated database per run; results committed to `eval/results/v1.json`.
179: - `src/swapdesk/checker.py` — deterministic per-outcome checks and global invariants, no LLM judge.
180: - `docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md` — a controlled live BEFORE/AFTER comparison of the D1 final-sale denial evidence path.
181: 
182: ## Documentation
183: 
184: | Doc                                                                  | Purpose                                                                                         |
185: | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
186: | [`docs/API_CONTRACT.md`](docs/API_CONTRACT.md)                         | Normative customer frontend contract (agent async path + legacy notes)                          |
187: | [`docs/build-plan.md`](docs/build-plan.md)                           | Full build plan (spec, not evidence)                                                            |
188: | [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md)         | LangGraph Studio runbook with evidence                                                          |
189: | [`docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md`](docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md) | Runner/harness evidence walk-through                                                            |
190: | [`docs/business/`](docs/business/)                                   | Business plan (MD/PDF) and financial model (XLSX) — figures are assumptions, not observed facts |
191: | [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md)                                       | Slice-by-slice build log and conventions                                                        |
192: 
193: ## Contributing
194: 
195: - Backend owns `src/swapdesk/` and `tests/`. Frontend owns `frontend/`.
196: - Keep tests deterministic; business logic stays callable without HTTP or a model.
197: - Record each slice in `hackathon.md` with the exact commands run and pass/fail counts.
198: - Never commit `.env`, databases, or real customer data. `.env.example` carries key names only.
199:

display.text:
# SwapDesk

SwapDesk arranges shoe exchanges for a fictional shop. A customer asks for a different size, and the system checks policy and stock, holds a replacement, creates a return and a mock label, then verifies the saved state. Every request ends in one of four outcomes: **exchange arranged**, **clarification required**, **policy denial**, or **human escalation**.

All data is synthetic. There are no payments, shipments, or real customers. This is a neatHack project built by a team of four.

## Repository layout

```text
frontend/          Next.js dashboard — live API integration, local demo fallback
src/swapdesk/      Python backend package — FastAPI, SQLite, LangGraph agent
eval/              Frozen benchmark, deterministic checker, and run harness
tests/             Deterministic pytest suite (no network, no model)
docs/              Build plan, runbooks, evidence, and business deliverables
hackathon.md       Slice-by-slice build log and team conventions
```

## The two halves

- **Backend** (`src/swapdesk/`) — the agent runtime. Policy checks, atomic stock reservation, idempotent operations, an append-only action journal, a LangGraph tool-using agent, and a FastAPI surface for frontend integration. Deterministic and network-free to test.
- **Frontend** (`frontend/`) — the ops dashboard (Mission Control, Inbox, Inventory, Integrations, Customer Simulation, ticket detail). It calls the live backend API through a same-origin proxy (`/v1/*` → FastAPI, configured in `frontend/next.config.ts`) and falls back to built-in demo state when the backend is unreachable. Its own README lives at [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md).

---

## Backend

### Features

- Atomic stock reservation with no oversell, safe under concurrent writers.
- Idempotent operations: same key plus same payload returns the saved result; same key plus different payload is rejected.
- Policy enforcement: delivered status, 30-day return window, final-sale excluded.
- One active exchange per order item, across cases.
- Append-only action journal for every committed or duplicate-routed operation.
- Full mock exchange lifecycle: reserve → return → label → arrange, plus hold release, cancel, escalation, cleanup recovery, and a read-only verification handoff.
- Demo-only failure injection (`faults.py`) with same-key recovery.
- A LangGraph tool-using agent (`langchain.agents.create_agent`, Gemini or a LiteLLM proxy): curated tools, bounded loop, budget-capped requests, file-backed checkpoints, database-derived outcomes, template replies.
- neatlogs wiring (workflow/tool spans, local capture without a key, export with one).

### Installation

Requires Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/adr1en360/SwapDesk.git
cd SwapDesk
uv sync
```

### Test

```bash
uv run pytest -q
```

The suite is deterministic — no network, no model keys, no LLM judge.

### Run the API and worker

```bash
uv run uvicorn swapdesk.api:app --port 8000
uv run python -m swapdesk.worker
```

Both share `SWAPDESK_DB` (default `swapdesk.db`); agent checkpoints live
at `<db>.agent-checkpoints.sqlite`. Interactive docs at
`http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` (generated from the implementation, always
in sync). Normative customer contract:
[`docs/API_CONTRACT.md`](docs/API_CONTRACT.md).

| Method & route                         | What it does                                              |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `POST /v1/agent/tickets`               | Accept an agent ticket, queue RUN-1, return 202 + status URL |
| `GET /v1/agent/cases/{id}`             | Execution status + verified outcome when available (404 unknown) |
| `GET /v1/agent/cases/{id}/timeline`    | Sanitized action/journal events with run ids (404 unknown) |
| `POST /v1/agent/cases/{id}/continue`   | Queue a continuation run, or report terminal unchanged (404/409/422) |
| `POST /v1/tickets`                     | Legacy deterministic demo path (201, benchmark use; frontend must not use it) |
| `GET /v1/cases/{id}`                   | Legacy deterministic status (frontend must not use it)    |
| `GET /v1/cases/{id}/timeline`          | Legacy deterministic timeline (frontend must not use it)  |
| `POST /v1/cases/{id}/continue`         | Legacy deterministic continuation (frontend must not use it) |
| `GET /v1/fixtures`                     | Synthetic orders, items, and policy for dropdowns         |
| `POST /v1/demo/faults`                 | Disabled (403) unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`     |
| `DELETE /v1/demo/faults`               | Disabled (403) unless `SWAPDESK_ENABLE_DEMO_FAULTS=1`     |
| `GET /v1/health`                       | Liveness probe                                            |

`POST /v1/agent/tickets` returns **202 accepted** with `case_id`,
`run_id`, `execution_status`, and `status_url` — never a completed
outcome. `execution_status` (`queued`/`running`/`waiting_input`/
`completed`/`failed`) is distinct from the business `outcome`
(`arranged`/`clarification`/`denial`/`escalation`, null until a run
completes). Malformed requests return 422, unknown cases 404,
submission conflicts or concurrent runs 409, disabled demo controls
403. A run is bounded by `SWAPDESK_AGENT_BUDGET` provider requests and
`SWAPDESK_RUN_TIMEOUT_S` wall-clock seconds; failed runs are never
retried automatically.

`POST /v1/tickets` remains the legacy deterministic demo path used by
benchmarks. The customer frontend must use `/v1/agent/*`. The agent
route accepts optional structured order fields as request data; the
customer message remains the primary input, and consent is recorded
only when explicitly supplied.

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/agent/tickets \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"message":"Exchange item ITEM-01 for size 42","order_id":"ORD-1001","order_item_id":"ITEM-01","size":"42"}'

curl localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx
curl localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx/timeline
curl -X POST localhost:8000/v1/agent/cases/CASE-xxx/continue \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"message":"42 is fine","consent_size":"42"}'
```

No authentication: this is a local mock. Agent status and timeline
reads are read-only and never block on the worker.

### Configuring the agent

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in what you have (`.env` is git-ignored; never commit it):

- `GEMINI_API_KEY` — direct Gemini access (no `LITELLM_API_KEY`).
- `LITELLM_API_KEY` — enables the hackathon LiteLLM proxy instead; `SWAPDESK_MODEL` then picks from `nova-micro`, `nova-lite`, `nova-pro`, `nova-2-lite`, `claude-haiku`, `claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-4.6` (default `claude-haiku`). Override the endpoint with `LITELLM_BASE_URL`.
- `SWAPDESK_MODEL` — Gemini model id when using Gemini directly (default `gemini-3.8-flash`).
- `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` + `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` — neatlogs telemetry export; local-only capture works without them.

Live model calls and telemetry export need working egress to the upstream APIs; where the network blocks them, the deterministic suites still pass.

### Inspecting the agent in LangGraph Studio

Two graphs share one architecture (`prepare` → nested `agent` subgraph → `verify`), defined in `src/swapdesk/agent/studio_flow.py` and served from `langgraph.json`:

```bash
uv run langgraph dev
```

Open Studio at `https://smith.langchain.com/studio/?baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8123`. Two assistants are registered:

- **`swapdesk_offline` (default).** A scripted model replays tool calls against the real backend — zero model requests. Proves the wiring, never Gemini's decisions.
- **`swapdesk_live` (opt-in).** Budget-capped Gemini. Needs `SWAPDESK_MODEL` plus `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or the LiteLLM pair) and a per-run budget; anything missing fails loudly before any model call.

Full runbook with evidence: [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md).

## Frontend

A Next.js 16 (Turbopack) App Router dashboard with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4.

### Run it

```bash
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
```

Other scripts: `npm run build` (production build), `npm run start`, `npm run lint`.

### Pages and demo flow

| Route           | Page                | What it demos                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `/`             | Mission Control     | Agent metrics + live execution queue                 |
| `/inbox`        | Inbox               | Sample ticket stream                                 |
| `/inventory`    | Inventory           | Stock levels that react to simulations               |
| `/database`     | Database Schema     | Tables the agent reads/writes                        |
| `/integrations` | Integrations        | Inbound webhook triggers (Zendesk, Shopify, Gorgias) |
| `/settings`     | Agent Settings      | Autonomy/guardrail config UI                         |
| `/simulate`     | Customer Simulation | Inject a customer complaint into the queue           |
| `/ticket/[id]`  | Ticket Execution    | Per-ticket action timeline                           |

The dashboard calls the backend through a same-origin proxy (`frontend/src/lib/api.ts` + a `next.config.ts` rewrite), and falls back to a client-side store (`frontend/src/store/swapdesk.tsx`) when the backend is offline. **Customer Simulation** runs a case in Deterministic (`POST /v1/tickets`) or Agent (`POST /v1/agent/tickets`) mode; **Inventory** renders the `GET /v1/fixtures` catalogue; **ticket detail** reads `GET /v1/cases/{id}` and its timeline; **Settings** arms/clears demo faults. **Reset Mock Data** (inventory page) restores the local demo state. Completion rate is computed from the queue and cost shows "Demo Mode".

SEO is configured across all routes (per-page metadata, generated Open Graph/Twitter images, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`). See [`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md) and [`frontend/setup.md`](frontend/setup.md) for details.

## Evaluation and evidence

- `eval/cases_v1.json` — frozen 30-case benchmark (`benchmark-v1`, 8 holdouts) covering arrangement, denial, clarification, and escalation, with seeded fault schedules.
- `eval/driver.py` — deterministic reference driver (not the agent) that exercises the cases.
- `eval/harness.py` + `eval/run.py` — isolated database per run; results committed to `eval/results/v1.json`.
- `src/swapdesk/checker.py` — deterministic per-outcome checks and global invariants, no LLM judge.
- `docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md` — a controlled live BEFORE/AFTER comparison of the D1 final-sale denial evidence path.

## Documentation

| Doc                                                                  | Purpose                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`docs/API_CONTRACT.md`](docs/API_CONTRACT.md)                         | Normative customer frontend contract (agent async path + legacy notes)                          |
| [`docs/build-plan.md`](docs/build-plan.md)                           | Full build plan (spec, not evidence)                                                            |
| [`docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md`](docs/STUDIO_VERIFICATION.md)         | LangGraph Studio runbook with evidence                                                          |
| [`docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md`](docs/EVIDENCE_RUNNER_HARNESS.md) | Runner/harness evidence walk-through                                                            |
| [`docs/business/`](docs/business/)                                   | Business plan (MD/PDF) and financial model (XLSX) — figures are assumptions, not observed facts |
| [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md)                                       | Slice-by-slice build log and conventions                                                        |

## Contributing

- Backend owns `src/swapdesk/` and `tests/`. Frontend owns `frontend/`.
- Keep tests deterministic; business logic stays callable without HTTP or a model.
- Record each slice in `hackathon.md` with the exact commands run and pass/fail counts.
- Never commit `.env`, databases, or real customer data. `.env.example` carries key names only.
